perf.summary: Replace `idx = (idx + 1) % this.Capacity` in the open-addressing probe loops with a branchless/branch wrap to remove an integer division per probe step.
perf.currentCost: Each probe iteration executes an integer `%` against a runtime `Capacity` that is not a compile-time power of two. Integer division/modulo is ~20-40 cycles on most ARM/x86 cores and cannot be strength-reduced by Burst since Capacity is a runtime value. This is the innermost hot loop of every Add/Find.
perf.proposedChange: Increment then wrap with a compare instead of modulo: `idx++; if (idx == this.Capacity) idx = 0;` (or the branchless form `idx++; idx -= (idx == this.Capacity ? this.Capacity : 0);`). Since idx starts in [0,Capacity) and increments by exactly 1, it can only ever equal Capacity, never exceed it, so a single equality test is exactly equivalent to `% Capacity`.
perf.rationale: Removes a full integer-division uop from the dependency chain of every probe step, replacing it with an add + predicated subtract (1-2 cycles). Linear probing typically does many steps near load, so this is a real per-step win.
perf.risk: Equivalent only because the step is exactly +1 and idx is always < Capacity before the step; holds for both loops here. No signed/overflow concern since Capacity << int.MaxValue.

perf.summary: `hash % (uint)Capacity` is an unavoidable division per lookup, but the (uint)Capacity cast and reciprocal can be precomputed once at construction.
perf.currentCost: GetFirstIdx runs once per TryAdd/Find/TryGetValue and does a 32-bit unsigned division by a runtime Capacity. Burst cannot fold this because Capacity is not const.
perf.proposedChange: Precompute and store `uint capacityU` (and optionally a libdivide-style magic/shift pair) at construction time alongside Capacity, and use it in GetFirstIdx and the wrap. At minimum cache `(uint)this.Capacity` to avoid the repeated cast; ideally store a precomputed multiply-shift reciprocal to turn the modulo into a mul+shift+sub.
perf.rationale: Division by a value known only at construction can be converted to a multiply+shift using a fixed reciprocal computed once, trading a ~25-cycle div for ~5 cycles on every hash lookup.
perf.risk: The full reciprocal path adds code/complexity and must be verified for the exact Capacity range; the cheap cast-caching variant is risk-free. Note Capacity could be 0 if TCapacity is too small for one element — division by zero is already a latent issue in current code, unchanged by this.

perf.summary: The `fixed` pin + pointer arithmetic for Ptr/NumItems/Keys/values is recomputed on every access inside the probe loops; hoist the base pointers into locals once per public call.
perf.currentCost: `this.Ptr` re-pins `&this.data` and recasts on every single dereference (`this.Ptr[idx]`, `this.Keys[idx]`, `this.NumItems[firstIdx]`, and value base in GetElementAt each recompute `capacity * (...)`). In the do/while loops Ptr is dereferenced once per iteration plus Keys per match, each going through a property getter with a fixed-statement.
perf.proposedChange: At the top of TryAdd/Find/TryGetValue, take `uint* hashes = this.Ptr; int* numItems = (int*)(hashes + Capacity); TKey* keys = (TKey*)(hashes + Capacity*2);` once, plus the value base pointer, and index those locals in the loop. Hoists the pin, the casts, and the `capacity * stride` multiply out of the per-iteration path.
perf.rationale: Eliminates a repeated pin + multiply + property-call from the hot probe loop, shortening the dependency chain and helping Burst keep the bases in registers. Pointers into the same fixed struct are stable for the call duration.
perf.risk: Pinning once for the whole method is semantically identical here since `data` is a struct field that does not move; just ensure all loop accesses use the hoisted locals so no GC-hole assumptions break (unmanaged blittable, so fine).

perf.summary: Per-bucket `NumItems` counter array (int per bucket) costs Capacity*4 bytes of the fixed storage and shrinks effective Capacity; reconsider whether it is needed or can be narrowed.
perf.currentCost: Layout is [uint hash][int numItems][TKey][TValue] per slot, so 4 bytes/slot go to NumItems. CalcCapacity divides total size by (4+4+key+value); the numItems word roughly halves capacity for small key/value types and adds a cache line touch (NumItems[firstIdx]) separate from the hashes array.
perf.proposedChange: If NumItems counts only collisions-into-this-home-bucket for early-out in Find, it can be a narrower type (byte/ushort) given Capacity is bounded, or removed in favor of probing until an empty slot (uint.MaxValue) as TryAdd already does. Narrowing to byte recovers 3 bytes/slot of capacity and packs counters into far fewer cache lines.
perf.rationale: Smaller per-slot footprint increases Capacity for the same TCapacity storage (better load factor / fewer probes) and reduces cache pressure; the counters also become contiguous and prefetch-friendly.
perf.risk: Removing NumItems changes Find's termination from count-based to empty-slot-based, altering probe counts for missing keys (still correct, but different perf profile and full-table-no-empty edge needs the existing do/while wrap guard). Narrowing requires proving max chain length < type max; behavior-preserving only if the counter cannot overflow, so byte/ushort must be chosen against the max possible Capacity.

perf.summary: Value-base offset `capacity * (sizeof(uint)+sizeof(int)+sizeof(TKey))` is recomputed every value access and uses `sizeof(int)` for the NumItems stride while NumItems is `int*` and hashes are `uint*` — keep the stride constants centralized to avoid drift and recompute.
perf.currentCost: The constant base offset (independent of idx) is multiplied out on every GetElementAt call; only `idx * sizeOfValueT` actually varies. Also the per-slot stride literal is duplicated between CalcCapacity (sizeof(uint)+sizeof(uint)+...) and GetElementAt (sizeof(uint)+sizeof(int)+...).
perf.proposedChange: Precompute the constant value-region base offset once at construction (or hoist per-call) and add only `idx * sizeOfValueT` at access time. Define the per-slot stride as a single computed field used by both CalcCapacity and the offset math to guarantee they agree.
perf.rationale: Removes a multiply from each value access and removes a duplicated/divergent magic expression, lowering both cycles and maintenance risk.
perf.risk: sizeof(int)==sizeof(uint)==4 so the two expressions are numerically identical today; centralizing is purely defensive and behavior-preserving. Caching the base offset is safe because Capacity and sizes are fixed after construction.
